summary: Manfred Mayrhofer was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Wilhelm Brandenstein at the University of Graz (Ph.D. ~1945–1949, Habilitation ~1949–1951). He held professorships at Saarland University (1962–1966) and the University of Vienna (1966–1990).

Manfred Taube, a scholar in Tibetology, Indology, and Central Asian studies, studied at the University of Leipzig (1949–1953) under Friedrich Weller. In 1991, he became Professor of Tibetan and Mongolian Philology at Leipzig.

Mangal Deva Shastri, an Indologist and linguist, earned his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (1919–1922) studying under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He later served as Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1937–1946).

Working in Buddhist studies and Indology, Manik Man Bajracharya studied at Tribhuvan University, HTW Berlin, and Metropolia University of Applied Sciences. He has been affiliated with the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2018–2026).
Manilal Patel was an Indology scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Marburg, where he studied under Johannes Nobel.

Manish Sinha, a specialist in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, earned his Ph.D. at Magadh University in 1999. He became a professor there in 1996 and served as department head from 2018 to 2021.

Buddhist studies scholar Manit Akkhachat studied at Ramkhamhaeng University (B.A. 2007–2009) and Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (Ph.D. 2017–2022). In 2013, he lectured at Nakhon Ratchasima Rajabhat University.

Manjiri Bhalerao, an Indology and archaeology scholar, studied at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth. She became an Associate Professor at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth in 2004.
Philosopher Manlio Iofrida studied at the University of Pisa and Scuola Normale Superiore (~1970–1974). He held posts at the University of Pisa (~1981–1992) and the University of Bologna (~1992).

Manshi Kiyozawa was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Fenollosa. He taught at several institutions and was the founding president of Otani University from 1901 to 1902.

Manu Leumann was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Strasbourg under Albert Thumb. He worked with the Thesaurus Linguae Latinae and served as professor at the University of Zurich (1927–1959).

id: P:Manuel Antonio Ato del Avellanal Carrera
summary: Manuel Antonio Ato del Avellanal Carrera studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara and SOAS University of London. He was a lecturer at the Pontifical Catholic University of Peru (2020) and Universidad del Pacífico (2023).

Manuel Sassmann is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Stuttgart and Heidelberg University. He serves as a Research Fellow at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

id: P:Manuel de la Revilla y Moreno
summary: Manuel de la Revilla y Moreno was a Spanish philosophy scholar who studied under Francisco García Ayuso at Complutense University of Madrid. He later served as Professor of Literary History at the Complutense University of Madrid in 1876.

Marbury Bladen Ogle studied at Johns Hopkins University under Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve and Maurice Bloomfield. He held classical language professorships and chairs at the University of Vermont, Ohio State University, and the University of Minnesota Twin Cities.

Marc Aurel Stein studied at the University of Tübingen (Ph.D. under Rudolf von Roth). A scholar of archaeology and Indology, he held posts at the University of the Punjab and the Archaeological Survey of India (1901–1929).
Marc Tiefenauer is an Indology scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Lausanne in 2016, studying under Johannes Bronkhorst and Nahid Rouzbeh.

Marc-Henri Deroche is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies under Matthew T. Kapstein, having also studied under Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, and Katsumi Mimaki.
Linguist Marcel Cohen studied under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi between 1905 and 1911. He later held posts at the University of Paris and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1919–1954).

Marcel Granet was a sinologist who studied under Émile Durkheim and Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and founded the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises.
